answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can rely on bonded stake that is slashable upon graph-based detection of identity clusters. Agents deposit capital into a shared pool; if peer monitoring identifies a porous karst of linked fakes, a gale of coordinated attestations triggers slashing. This makes the attacker cost spiral upward, as each additional identity requires proportionally more locked value that is at risk of total loss once the cluster is exposed.
